## Rule

Two-background plaid with marker colors. The input contains two dominant
background colors and rare marker colors. Each marker sits on one of the two
background classes. The output draws both diagonal families through every
marker; cells on those diagonals are recolored by the marker color associated
with the cell's underlying background class. The live solver still implements
this as a 266-exemplar lookup rather than a dynamic geometric rule.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

- ~~Do not spend worker time on task324 public-LB rewrites without a new nonzero-weight diagnostic.~~ **OVERTURN 2026-05-23**: cherry13b 0.00 = LIVE wrong on hidden, not zero latent weight. Structural rewrite STAGED.
- Do not replace the sorted-tier int64 color-grid assembly with direct F32 one-hot `ScatterND`; it verified but regressed to 99,447 cost under official memory accounting.
- The 44,417 candidate uses `ArgMax(input) > 0` as the active-region mask. Visible+arc-gen has no active color 0. If private examples can use active color 0, use a robust active-sum variant despite the higher cost.
- ORT wraps negative OneHot indices Python-style (`-1 → depth-1 = 9`), contradicting ONNX spec (which says all-zeros for negative). Do not use OneHot with index `-1` as a "no-op" sentinel; use `eye_10 Gather` instead or pass input as the Where false-branch.
- Using OneHot as an intermediate (not final) node risks padding cell bleed: `ArgMax(all-zeros) = 0`, `OneHot(0) = ch0=1.0`, but padding cells must be all-zeros. The eye_10 Gather trick for one-hot + input-as-Where-false-branch is the safe pattern.
- **v5b's 3-way vote CAN be dropped — but only with the right base-vs-stripe disambiguation (2026-05-31).** Naive drops fail: (a) `plaid_bg0=(bg0_row>0)AND(bg0_col>0)` → **88/266** (`bg0`=most-common is the STRIPE color when stripes are dense, so base-assuming formulas invert); (b) v5b's plaid sub-vote alone → **250/266**. ✅ **SOLVED by compress_v3**: the base color B = the bg color in the **top-left 2×2 corner** (always base, since `brows`/`bcols` start at `randint(2,7)≥2`); then `on_base=(countB_row>0)AND(countB_col>0)` is EXACT → 266/266 + 100% vs ground truth (v5b ~98.5%). Lesson: the corner is the cheap exact anchor for which-color-is-the-base; the per-cell vote is unnecessary once B is pinned.
- **mc-detection no-marker default = color 0, not blank** (compress_v1): when mirroring v5b's `Gather(eye_10, mc_i)` recolor in single-channel index space, a no-marker class gives `ReduceMax=0`; v5b paints color 0 there (`eye_10[0]`), so clamp `Max(ReduceMax, 1)` in +1 space. Without it: 37/2000 arcgen + 844/2000 adversarial divergences (the vote mis-buckets markers, emptying a class on *valid* inputs). See traps.md §14g.
- **Do NOT merge Sho's 2-channel factored diagonal conv to 1 channel** (2026-07-12 worker3, `build_task324_w3_diag1ch.py`): merging `w1`/`w2` to 1 X-shaped channel to delete 400 B → **0/266 visible**. Cross-terms `w2[\]⊛s1[/]` + `w2[/]⊛s1[\]` render spurious diagonals. The 2 channels (one per diagonal family) are FORCED. See `hard_records/wall_factored_conv_floor_2026-07-12.md`.
- **Do NOT re-factor the diagonal conv to fewer params with an EVEN 2nd-stage kernel** (2026-07-12 worker3, `build_task324_w3_diag96.py`): `w1[2,1,9,9]`+`w2[1,2,6,6]`dil6 = 234p (−26 vs 260, would be 7872) has a **byte-identical effective 39×39 X kernel** but → **163/266 visible FAIL**. Even `k2` has no center tap; `s1` truncation at the 20×20 boundary then leaves diagonal cells near a corner marker unlit (they need offset-0/±1/±2 taps that an even, spacing-6 stage2 lacks). **`k2` must be ODD → 260 params is the proven diagonal-render floor.**
- **Do NOT revert to a single 39×39 X-conv** (2026-07-12 worker3 pass2, `build_task324_w3_singleX.py`): deletes `s1` (−800 B) but the dense `xk[1,1,39,39]` costs +1521p → **266/266 visible but profile 8359 (mem 6811 + params 1548), +461 REGRESSION** vs Sho 7898 (`ng_graph_cost_diff` verified). The factored `s1` (800 B) BEATS the dense kernel (1261p). Sho's 2-stage factored conv is the diagonal floor; the old "X-conv 1521p is the floor" note is refuted.
